key_insight: LLM stakeholder agents can generate healthcare decision weights, but deliberation and option order can distort preferences enough to change optimization outcomes.
engineering_relevance: Healthcare decision-support systems should audit LLM-generated weights and model their uncertainty rather than rely only on average preferences.
method: Elicit explicit criterion ratings for outpatient scheduling from stakeholder-role agents.
Infer implicit trade-offs from pairwise emergency department configuration choices and test presentation-order effects.
Use robust weighted-sum optimization to account for preference uncertainty.
evidence_signal: Computational experiments found role- and condition-sensitive explicit ratings, strong presentation-order effects in pairwise choices, and robust solutions that differed from average-weight solutions in most cases.
watch_item: Context-aware choice models showed limited evidence of outperforming an order-only model on unseen comparison pairs, raising concerns about interpreting choices as stable preferences.
paper_title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
